relevance_note: A somatic-mutation cohort study that describes four patients with somatic TNFAIP3 mutations at individual level: "We reported the first four patients with HA20 with somatic TNFAIP3 mutations."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and copied table cells verbatim. Scope: of 2,912 cohort patients, four (P23-P26) carry somatic TNFAIP3 mutations; all other Table 1 patients (UBA1, KRAS, NRAS, NLRP3, CARD14, NFKBIA, NLRC4, STING1) are out of scope. Table 1 is a rotated table whose Markdown conversion is badly garbled: patients are columns, row labels are shifted, and cells spill into neighbouring columns and rows. I read the continuation table (P15-P30) by column index, using the Patient ID row (P23 = data column 8, P24 = 9, P25 = 10, P26 = 11) and accepted a value only where it sits in that patient's own column; P24 and P26 are also tied to TNFAIP3 by the Figure 3 legend. Variants: column 8 holds 'NM_001270508.2: c.130_137del:' (P23) and column 9 'c.577G>T; E193*' (P24, after a spilled 'p.R45Tfs*53'). Column 10 holds two variants, 'NM_001270508.2: c.820delC' and 'NM_001270508.2: c.1156A>T; K386*', and 'p.P274Hfs*13' sits in the WES VAF row of column 11; column 11 (P26) holds no variant. Under the no-positional-reading rule (D-31) I did not split column 10 between P25 and P26: both have variant rows with variant 'not reported'. The protein 'p.R45Tfs*53' spilled into P24's column, so P23's protein is left null. Sex: column 11 reads 'Female (type III) sclerosis Female' (P26 and the next patient); both values are female, so P26 is recorded female. Clinical symptoms: P23 'Frequent diarrhea' (column 8, after P22's spilled 'lupus nephritis'), P24 'Recurrent oral ulcers' (column 9), P25 oral ulcers (column 10 holds 'Recurrent ... oral ulcers' and 'Severe oral ulcers three or four times once a year', both oral ulcers but possibly one of them P26's). P26 gets no symptom because nothing sits in its column; the text's 'Three patients presented with oral ulcers, and one patient experienced recurrent diarrhea' gives counts without names and was not used to assign. Ages ('Age at sampling, y') are scrambled between the Patient ID and age rows and left not reported; sampling age is not an onset or last-evaluation age anyway. Zygosity 'mosaic' from the named group of four patients with somatic TNFAIP3 mutations; pathogenicity from the statement on pathogenic somatic mutations in TNFAIP3; variant type not stated per variant (Figure 2D gives only cohort-level types). Not given rows: the 'affected children' to whom gonosomal mosaicism was transmitted 'in three of these families' are described only collectively (pedigrees in Figure 3A, not in the text), so neither their number nor their parent is known; and the previously published 'healthy individual with no symptoms' with somatic TNFAIP3 mutations (ref 44) is mentioned in passing without a variant, sex or age. is_proband left null: the text says samples came 'from the probands' without saying which people are probands in the four families. cites_prior_report is true because the paper says patient P34 (NLRC4, out of scope) was reported previously (ref 15); it does not say this for the TNFAIP3 patients. Text 'recurrent diarrhea' versus table 'Frequent diarrhea' is a wording difference, not a contradiction.
